demos.title: Sample scans
demos.hint: Real public scans, plus one of our own. The public ones are captures of real places, so they land on the model rather than lining up with it. The Poblenou survey is written in the same CRS as its models and lines up exactly.
demos.failed: That sample could not be downloaded. Check your connection and try again.

items.autzen: Aerial LiDAR over a stadium, with true colour and ground/unclassified returns. LASzip-compressed and recorded in feet — both handled on the way in.
items.redRocks: Four million points of a sandstone amphitheatre, coloured from the survey's own photographs — the closest thing here to a photograph you can fly through. Colour is all it carries: no classes, no intensity. 10 MB, so give it a moment.
items.sampleC: The most complete file of the set in half a megabyte: true colour, intensity and eight classification codes at once. The one to load when you want to flip through every Colour by mode.
items.newMexico: A LAS 1.4 ground survey in US survey feet. Good for checking the newer point format reads correctly.
items.mvk: Small and instant, with six classification codes — the quickest way to see Colour by → Classification.
items.loneStar: A geyser cone scanned from the ground, stored as a Cloud Optimized Point Cloud. Its octree is read coarsest-first, so the whole cone is there immediately and then sharpens.
items.tabletop: Boxes on a wooden table, close enough to read the packaging: the colour came off a camera rather than being assigned. It carries a label per point too, so Classification separates the objects from the table.
items.indoorRoom: A room corner in that same photographic colour, at room scale rather than object scale — the nearest thing here to what an as-built scan of an interior actually looks like.
items.warsaw: A tiny coloured sample. Loads in a blink; useful for trying the appearance controls.
items.poblenou: Our own survey of the Poblenou Pavilion plot, written in the same projected CRS as the model. Load it with any of the three Poblenou disciplines and it lands on them — the one pair here that can show a scan lining up with a model instead of merely sitting near it. Synthetic, generated alongside the models.
items.cras: A real 21-scan TLS capture of FEUP laboratories with its corresponding as-built IFC. RGB, intensity and 33 semantic classes; rigidly aligned and published under CC BY 4.0.

transport.title: Simulated binary channel
transport.hint: Loss, reorder and latency are simulated; the CRC parser and three-frame buffer are the real ingest path.

status.truncated: Stopped at {{count}} points — the file holds more than this viewer keeps in memory at once.
status.noModel: No IFC model loaded — the scan is placed on its own.
status.partial: Part of this scan could not be read and is missing from the view. What you see is incomplete.
status.budgetHint: Points the loaded scans keep in memory, including scans still loading. A scan that does not fit waits while another scan is still loading; otherwise it loads truncated, or is refused when the budget is full. Streamed COPC clouds are not counted: the Detail setting bounds them.

align.title: Alignment
align.crsNone: The scan file declares no coordinate reference system.

reason.sameCrs: The scan and the model use the same coordinate reference system.
reason.assumedSameCrs: The model gives grid coordinates but names no CRS — the scan's was assumed to match.
reason.reprojected: The scan was reprojected from its own grid into the model's.
reason.ifcCrsUnknown: The model names a CRS this build cannot resolve; the scan's grid was used directly.
reason.noElevationDatum: The model declares no reference elevation — heights may be offset vertically.
reason.geographicAnchor: Aligned through the model's site latitude/longitude, which is coarser than a map conversion.
reason.groundMatched: The scan's floor was placed on the model's floor.
reason.sharedLocalFrame: Neither file is georeferenced, but the two occupy the same local coordinates.
reason.noCommonReference: Nothing links the two files, so the scan was centred on the model. Use the offsets below to place it.
reason.cloudCrsUnknown: The scan names a coordinate system this build has no definition for, so its georeferencing could not be used. Paste a proj4 definition below to unlock it.
reason.sceneAnchorSameGrid: Placed by its CRS against the first georeferenced scan (same grid, no reprojection).
reason.sceneAnchorReprojected: Placed by its CRS against the scene anchor, reprojected through WGS84.
reason.assumedVerticalDatum: All scans are assumed to share one height datum — the file does not state it.

align.manualWarning: This placement is a starting point, not a measurement.

crsForm.title: Coordinate system
crsForm.hint: Find the definition for {{code}} at epsg.io and paste the proj4 line.
crsForm.invalid: proj4 could not parse that definition.
crsForm.applied: Definition accepted — the scan was re-aligned.

align.upAxisGuessed: Not stated by the file — inferred from the shape of the scan. If the scan is lying on its side, switch it.

transform.title: Adjust placement
transform.hint: Offsets are applied on top of the detected alignment and are never folded into it.

display.title: Appearance
display.densityHint: How many points are drawn at once. Lower this if navigation stutters.
display.confidenceHint: Hides points the reconstruction was least sure about. Only files that carry a per-point confidence have this.

inspect.title: Inspect
inspect.hint: Reads one point from the scan: where it is, and what the file recorded there.
inspect.none: No point under the cursor. Try closer to a dense area.

unsupported.e57: E57 is not supported yet. Export the scan as LAS or PLY from your scanner software.
unsupported.proprietary: That is a scanner-native project file. Export it as LAS or PLY first.
unsupported.unknown: That file type is not a point cloud this viewer can read.

error.notLas: This does not look like a LAS file.
error.notPly: This does not look like a PLY file.
error.plyNoXyz: The PLY file has no x/y/z vertex properties.
error.plyLayout: This PLY stores its vertices in a layout the reader cannot address.
error.plyMalformed: The PLY header could not be read.
error.noPoints: No points were found in the file.
error.malformedHeader: The file header is truncated or malformed.
error.headerFailed: The file header could not be read.
error.parseFailed: The file could not be read.
error.readerInit: No reader is available for that format.
error.workerFailed: The point cloud worker stopped unexpectedly.
error.timeout: The file did not start reading in time.
error.budgetExhausted: The point budget is full. Remove a scan before loading another.
error.lazDecode: The compressed point data could not be decoded. The file may be truncated or use a LASzip variant this decoder does not handle.
error.lazTooLarge: That LAZ is too large to decompress in a browser tab. Crop or decimate it first — see the docs for a PDAL one-liner.
error.lazOutOfMemory: Not enough memory to decompress that LAZ. Close other tabs, or crop the file first.
error.notCopc: This file has no Cloud Optimized Point Cloud index. If it is plain LAZ, rename it without the copc part.
error.copcDecode: The COPC octree could not be decoded. The file may be truncated or written to a different revision of the spec.
error.copcNoNodes: The COPC index is empty — the file declares an octree with no populated nodes.
error.copcOutOfMemory: Not enough memory to decode that COPC node.
error.pcdNoXyz: The PCD file has no x/y/z fields.
error.pcdEncoding: That PCD uses a data encoding this reader does not handle.
error.pcdCompressed: The compressed PCD body could not be decoded. The file may be truncated.
error.pcdMalformed: The PCD header could not be read.
error.alignFailed: The scan was read, but its placement could not be worked out. It has been left unplaced.

ui.startHint: Drop one or several files — each loads in parallel and can be removed on its own.
ui.replayTeaserHint: Four simulated scan timelines aligned with their models.
ui.qualityHint: Points drawn per frame. Higher looks denser but needs a faster GPU.

diag.title: Check-up
diag.allGood: Everything looks right with this scan.

issue.failed: This file could not be opened.
issue.partial: Part of the scan could not be read — what you see is incomplete.
issue.truncated: Only part of the file fits in memory, so the scan was cut short.
issue.upAxisGuessed: The file does not say which way is up. If it looks like it is lying on its side, flip it.
issue.colorUnavailable: The file has no data for the current colour mode, so it draws flat.
issue.faint: Opacity is so low the scan is barely visible.
issue.farFromModel: The scan is far away from the model.
issue.manualPlacement: Nothing links this scan to the model — it was centred on it. Check the placement.
issue.crsUnknown: The scan's coordinate system is unknown to this build, so its georeference was ignored.
issue.tooLarge: The scan is far larger than expected — the file is probably in millimetres, centimetres or feet.
issue.tooSmall: The scan is far smaller than expected — it may be in kilometres or scaled down.
issue.heavy: A lot of points at full detail — lighter settings will keep navigation smooth.

help.title: What do you see?
help.hint: Pick the symptom — each button applies the usual fix, and every fix can be undone from Appearance or Placement.

sideways.label: It is lying on its side

invisible.label: I can't see it
invisible.hint: Shows it and frames the camera

wrongSize.label: Huge or tiny
wrongSize.hint: Pick the unit the file was written in

colours.label: Black, white or odd colours
colours.hint: Cycles to a mode the file supports

slow.label: It's slow
slow.hint: Draws fewer points while you move

help.brokenTips: LAS / LAZ / COPC / PLY / PCD / XYZ / PTS / CSV read here. E57 and scanner projects (RCP, FLS, LSPROJ) must be exported to LAS or PLY first. Some LAZ files use a LASzip variant browsers cannot decode — re-save them as LAS or COPC. Very large files: crop or decimate them first.

recipes.title: Use cases
recipes.hint: One click sets up the view for a real task. Every filter below stays editable, and nothing changes the scan itself.

floorPlan.label: Floor plan cut
floorPlan.hint: Keeps a 60 cm band at the picked height (or 1.2 m above the lowest point) and looks from above — walls read like a drawing.

terrain.label: Terrain & contours
terrain.hint: Colours by height, draws contour lines and keeps only ground returns when the file is classified.

vegetation.label: Remove vegetation & noise
vegetation.hint: Hides the vegetation and noise classes so buildings, roads and ground stand out. Needs a classified file.

slab.label: Slab flatness
slab.hint: Click a point on the slab: keeps a thin band around it and draws a line every 1 cm, so bumps and dips show as rings.

scanVsBim.label: Scan vs BIM
scanVsBim.hint: Draws the scan in one bright colour over a translucent model, so anything built off-design sticks out. Needs an IFC model.

clearance.label: Measure a clearance
clearance.hint: Turns on the distance tool: click two points of the scan — floor to beam, wall to wall — to read the real, as-built gap.

analyze.pickFirst: Click a point on the scan first — Inspect is on.
analyze.activeBanner: Analysis filters are hiding part of the scan.

slice.title: Height slice
slice.hint: Heights are scene metres. Pair it with Measure to read clear heights, or with a top view to trace a floor plan.

contours.title: Contour lines
contours.hint: Coarse steps read terrain; 1–2 cm steps reveal a slab that is not flat.

classes.title: Classes
classes.hint: Tap a class to hide or show it. Codes follow the ASPRS LAS standard.

measure.title: Measure the scan
measure.hint: Scans snap like models do: distances, areas and angles land on real points.
